title: The tree
dek: Derrick's ancestry as it now stands, graded on the five-word ladder the sibling archives share.

legend.label: Documented
legend.what: A record was read, and it says this.

legend.label: Probable
legend.what: The evidence points one way and nothing points the other.

legend.label: Inferred
legend.what: Reasoned from what is known, not witnessed in a record.

legend.label: Family
legend.what: Told, remembered, or written on somebody's family chart — not sourced.

legend.label: Disputed
legend.what: Two sources disagree and neither has been ruled out.

legend.label: Not established
legend.what: NOT A LEVEL ON THE LADDER. There is no claim here yet — the gap is drawn as a person so it stays visible.

legend.label: Ruled out
legend.what: NOT A LEVEL EITHER. A claim that was tested and failed, kept on the tree because deleting it would hide the work.

people.name: Lynn Derrick Luwinski
people.how: Named only. No dates, no age, nothing that could be worked backwards into one — the archive's standing rule for anyone alive.

people.name: Leonard Aubrey Robert Wear
people.how: THE WEAKEST LINK ON THE TREE, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT. The DNA proves descent from Henry Robert Wear and Martha Maud Castle as a couple — 253 cM in twelve regions no Castle cousin shares. The birth index gives that couple two sons: one thirty-one in June 1948 and one eleven. NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES LEONARD AS ANYBODY'S FATHER. His death year is itself unresolved: 1973 has failed three separate tests and 1979 rests on a single transcription.

people.name: Ivone de Figueiredo
people.dates: b. 4 March 1924, Lourenço Marques · d. Porto
people.how: Recorded under six spellings of her maiden surname, three forenames and five married names. Married Johannes Antonie Oelofse de Witt (Feb 1948), Kurt Luwinski (June 1948) and Morris Isaac Salkow (Feb 1953).

people.name: Kurt Israel Luwinski
people.how: Ivone's husband when Derrick was born, and not his biological father. EXCLUDED TWICE OVER BY DNA: 0.0% Ashkenazi where a quarter would be required, and a Y haplogroup, R-S11477, that is North Sea rather than Ashkenazi. He stays on the tree because he is the reason the question was ever asked.

people.name: Henry Robert Wear
people.dates: b. Q3 1889, St Olave Bermondsey · d. 11 September 1969, Johannesburg
people.how: Birth index vol 1D p230. Hertfordshire Regiment, service no. 3010. Sailed London–Cape on the Durban Castle, 5 April 1939, occupation machine minder. Buried West Park.

people.name: Martha Maud Castle
people.dates: b. 21 July 1895, Baldock · d. 16 March 1986, Johannesburg
people.how: Baptised at Baldock 22 September 1895. Married Henry Robert Wear at Hitchin in October 1914. Sailed London–Durban on the Dunvegan Castle, 10 August 1939, with four children. Buried West Park. HER EXACT DATE OF BIRTH CAME FROM a second-cousin match'S TREE ON 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — this archive had only the year.

people.name: Ivone's father and mother
people.how: THE OLDEST UNSOLVED QUESTION IN THIS ARCHIVE. Their surnames are known from the 1948 divorce file — she is recorded as born MOTA FIGUEIREDO — but not their given names. Her 1924 Lourenço Marques birth registration and her Porto death record would each name both outright.

people.name: Robert Wear
people.dates: b. c. 1859, Bermondsey · d. Q1 1890, St Olave Southwark, aged 31
people.how: Married Emma Hawkins Q4 1881, St Olave Southwark, vol 1D p455. Died vol 1D p141 — six months after his son was born. The boy never knew him.

people.name: Emma Hawkins
people.dates: b. 7 February 1859, Aldenham · d. Q2 1944, Hitchin, aged 85
people.how: A widow at thirty-two and TWICE WIDOWED BY 1939. Robert Wear died in 1890; by 1891 she had taken her three children home to her brother's house at Watford. She then married JOHN HULL, a railway labourer, and had two more children, ALBERT J in 1895 and EDITH M in 1897 — so Henry Robert was raised from about four by a stepfather. AND SHE OUTLIVED THAT HUSBAND TOO. The 1939 Register finds her at 63 PIX ROAD, LETCHWORTH, aged eighty, WIDOWED, and INCAPACITATED — BLIND, living with her daughter Louisa and son-in-law William Shenton. HER SON HENRY ROBERT HAD RAISED HIS OWN SIX CHILDREN AT 72 PIX ROAD, THE SAME STREET. Her exact date of birth comes from that register, which is a woman of eighty giving it to a registrar. HER LIFE NOW RUNS END TO END, closed 17 September. EMMA HULL DIED IN THE SECOND QUARTER OF 1944, registered at Hitchin, aged eighty-five — five years after the register found her blind at Pix Road, and four years after the grandson she would have known as a boy was taken prisoner in the desert. Eighty-five years from Aldenham to Letchworth, two husbands buried, five children, and thirty miles.

people.name: George William Castle × Caroline Wallis
people.dates: he 1862–1916 · she b. 28 February 1863, d. 1957 — married October 1882, Hitchin
people.place: Willian → Norton End → Middle Row, Baldock
people.how: REGRADED 16 September from DOCUMENTED to PROBABLE, and the demotion is the point. The marriage, the nine children and the dates came from another researcher's tree, not from records this archive has read. WHAT IS DOCUMENTED, because the 1871 census was pulled and read here, is that a GEORGE CASTLE, 30, agricultural labourer, was living at Norton End as SON-IN-LAW to James Giddins with a son George, 8. WHAT IS NOT is the birthplace at Willian, the October 1882 marriage, and the nine children — all still one tree's word. The census also disagrees with that tree twice: it gives the boy's birthplace as BALDOCK, not Willian, and his birth year as 1863, not 1862. Under the ladder that is exactly what PROBABLE means — the evidence points one way and nothing points the other, but nobody has read the record that would settle it. The marriage certificate would. AND HER LATER LIFE IS NO LONGER A BLANK, found 17 September. SHE REMARRIED. Q3 1920 at Hitchin, vol 3A p2077: CAROLINE CASTLE married JAMES JAMES, four years after George William died. FROM 1920 SHE WAS CAROLINE JAMES, WHICH IS WHY NOBODY COULD FOLLOW HER — every tree that carries her as Caroline Wallis is hunting a death registered under another surname. The 1939 Register has her at 38 NORTON ROAD, BALDOCK, WIDOWED AGAIN at 76, RG101/1598B/017/25, AND IT GIVES HER EXACT DATE OF BIRTH: 28 FEBRUARY 1863, not the 1862 every secondary source repeats. She died in 1957, registered at Hitchin, as CAROLINE JAMES. AND THE 1921 CENSUS PROVES IT RATHER THAN INFERRING IT, found 17 September. There is no Caroline Castle in Hertfordshire in 1921 at all — she has gone out of the surname exactly when the index says she changed it. There is one CAROLINE JAMES: RG15 piece 07079, schedule 125, 9 BOSCOMBE PLACE, LETCHWORTH, 19 June 1921, wife of JAMES JAMES, born at WESTON, HERTFORDSHIRE. AND THE TWO CHILDREN IN THE HOUSE ARE ENUMERATED AS HIS STEP-CHILDREN AND CARRY THE SURNAME CASTLE: ERNEST ALBERT CYRIL CASTLE and FLORENCE MARGARITE HILDA CASTLE — the Ernest and Hilda of 1911, with their full names for the first time. A step-son in a census is a registrar's word for a remarriage, and it turns a GRO index line into a household. Her age is given as 56 years 4 months, which puts her birthday in FEBRUARY and so agrees with the 28th; the year is two out, and she is the one who said it. AND SHE HAD MOVED TO LETCHWORTH, which is where her daughter Martha Maud was raising the Wears.

people.name: William Wear
people.how: SADLER in 1851, harness maker by 1871 — the same trade, and the one his three eldest sons took up. In 1851 he heads a household at SALISBURY STREET, BERMONDSEY with his wife and two small boys; by 1871 he is at Jamaica Road with four sons, three of them at his own bench. HIS BIRTHPLACE IS GIVEN AS WALWORTH IN 1851 AND NEWINGTON IN 1871, which is not a contradiction — Walworth is a district inside Newington parish — but Walworth is the more precise and is where a baptism should be looked for.

people.name: Sarah Bloom
people.how: HER BIRTHPLACE IS DISPUTED BETWEEN TWO CENSUSES AND THEY ARE NOT EVEN IN THE SAME COUNTY. The 1851 return gives DEPTFORD, KENT; the 1871 gives BERMONDSEY, SURREY. That is not a spelling variant. Her maiden name is not in either — a married woman's never is — and comes instead from her son Robert's birth registration, which gives the mother's maiden name as BLOOM, corroborated by a seventeen-year-old niece named SARAH ANN BLOOM, born YARMOUTH, NORFOLK, living in the house on census night 1871. WITH A NORFOLK NIECE AND TWO NORFOLK MARRIAGES IN THE INDEX, the Blooms may not be a London family at all. Marked probable rather than documented until one record settles where she was born.

people.name: John Hawkins
people.how: AGRICULTURAL LABOURER. Eight in the household in 1871, every one of them born in the same parish.

people.name: Emma Hawkins
people.how: Her daughter Emma, twelve and a scholar in 1871, would marry in London, bury a husband there, and come home. CORRECTED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS ARCHIVE'S. A script that matched people BY NAME wrote the younger Emma's dates and history over this entry, because mother and daughter carry the same name and the code did not look at the generation. For part of a day this page said that a woman born about 1822 was born on 7 February 1859 and was blind at Letchworth in 1939. SHE IS THE MOTHER. The Pix Road entry belongs to her daughter, one row up. A match on a name is not a match on a person, which is the whole reason this archive keeps saying so about census indexes, and it said it while doing it.

people.name: George Castle × Martha Giddings
people.how: PROVED 16 September from the censuses themselves, having been taken on trust from another researcher's tree that morning. THE 1871 CENSUS AT NORTON END — RG10/1365 f.27 — has GEORGE CASTLE, 30, AGRICULTURAL LABOURER, ENUMERATED AS SON-IN-LAW in the house of James and Elizabeth Giddins, with his boy GEORGE CASTLE, 8, AS GRANDSON. Martha herself is not there; she had been dead eight years. BUT THE TWO RELATIONSHIPS ONLY WORK THROUGH HER, and they are the census's own words rather than a tree's. She died in the THIRD QUARTER of 1863 — Hitchin, volume 3A page 188 — and her son had been baptised that January, so she had something under a year with him, and her widower took the child to HER parents rather than his own.

people.name: James Giddins × Elizabeth Giddins
people.how: NEW ON 16 SEPTEMBER, and they are the reason this branch of the family stayed in Hertfordshire. He an AGRICULTURAL LABOURER born at Baldock; she born at Norton and, in 1871, doing PLATTING — straw-plaiting, the cottage industry that kept Hertfordshire women in work for a century. Found in both the 1861 census (RG9/816 f.69) and the 1871 (RG10/1365 f.27), at the same address a decade apart, with children George 1847, John 1849 and Emma 1855 — and, in 1871, a widowed son-in-law and a grandson who was not theirs to raise and whom they raised. WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY, a sentence added here that said their daughter Emma was born on 7 February 1859. THAT IS EMMA HAWKINS OF ALDENHAM, A DIFFERENT WOMAN IN A DIFFERENT PARISH. The Emma in this house is EMMA GIDDINS, born about 1855 at Norton, and the only thing the two share is a forename. Two Emmas, forty miles and four years apart, and this archive joined them in one sentence without looking at either.

people.name: William Wear's parents · Sarah Bloom's parents · the elder Hawkinses' · the elder Castles' and Giddingses'
people.how: ALL BORN BEFORE CIVIL REGISTRATION BEGAN IN 1837. From here it stops being an index problem and becomes a parish-register one — a different kind of search, in a different kind of archive.
